Runs the specified task(s). Falls back to the "default" task if no task name was specified, or lists
all tasks if an unknown task name was specified.

Usage: task [flags...] [task...] [-- CLI_ARGS...]

Arguments:
  [TASK]...      Task names to run, plus `VAR=value` overrides
  [CLI_ARGS]...  Arguments after `--`, passed to the task as `CLI_ARGS`

Options:
      --version
          Show Task version
  -h, --help
          Shows Task usage
      --init
          Creates a new Taskfile.yml in the current folder
      --completion <SHELL>
          Generates shell completion script
      --schema
          Prints the JSON Schema for Taskfiles to stdout
  -l, --list
          Lists tasks with description of current Taskfile
  -a, --list-all
          Lists tasks with or without a description
  -j, --json
          Formats task list as JSON
      --sort <SORT>
          Changes the order of the tasks when listed. [default|alphanumeric|none]
      --nested
          Nest namespaces when listing tasks as JSON
  -w, --watch
          Enables watch of the given task
  -v, --verbose
          Enables verbose mode
  -s, --silent
          Disables echoing
      --disable-fuzzy
          Disables fuzzy matching for task names
  -y, --yes
          Assume "yes" as answer to all prompts
      --interactive
          Prompt for missing required variables
  -p, --parallel
          Executes tasks provided on command line in parallel
  -n, --dry
          Compiles and prints tasks in the order that they would be run, without executing them
      --status
          Show fingerprint status of the given task(s)
      --summary
          Show summary about a task
  -x, --exit-code
          Pass-through the exit code of the task command
  -d, --dir <DIR>
          Sets the directory in which Task will execute and look for a Taskfile
  -t, --taskfile <TASKFILE>
          Choose which Taskfile to run. Defaults to "Taskfile.yml"
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Sets output style: [interleaved|group|prefixed]
      --output-group-begin <OUTPUT_GROUP_BEGIN>
          Message template to print before a task's grouped output
      --output-group-end <OUTPUT_GROUP_END>
          Message template to print after a task's grouped output
      --output-group-error-only
          Swallow output from successful tasks
  -c, --color
          Colored output. Enabled by default. Set --no-color or NO_COLOR=1 to disable
      --no-color
          Disables colored output
  -C, --concurrency <CONCURRENCY>
          Limit number of tasks to run concurrently [default: 0]
  -I, --interval <INTERVAL>
          Interval to watch for changes (e.g. 500ms, 1s)
  -F, --failfast
          When running tasks in parallel, stop all tasks if one fails
  -g, --global
          Runs global Taskfile, from $HOME/{T,t}askfile.{yml,yaml}
  -f, --force
          Forces execution of the directly called task
      --force-all
          Forces execution of the called task and all its dependent tasks
      --export-cache <PATH>
          Exports generated files and fingerprint state to a zip file
      --import-cache <PATH>
          Imports generated files and fingerprint state from a zip file
      --migrate
          Converts the Taskfile(s) from Go template syntax to native Jinja and adds a `templater:
          jinja` marker. Prints the result by default; use --write to apply in place. Targets the
          given file paths, or the resolved Taskfile
      --write
          With --migrate, rewrites the file(s) in place instead of printing
      --update[=<VERSION>]
          Replaces this task binary with a published GitHub release build: the latest release, or
          `--update=<VERSION>` for a specific one (an older one downgrades). Prints what it is about
          to install and asks before touching anything, unless --yes is given; the download is
          checked against the digest published beside it and must report its own version before it
          replaces the running binary. A symlinked install has its target replaced. Needs write
          access to the directory task is installed in. Exit: 0 up to date, installed, or declined;
          1 a newer release is available (--check); 2 the update or check itself failed
      --check
          With --update, reports whether a newer release is available and exits, downloading and
          installing nothing

Run 'task --list-all' to see the available tasks.
